The 2022 Ram 1500 Lone Star engages the driver with a steering system tuned for confident response and a chassis that feels planted through corners, making every drive more than routine. The well-weighted leather steering wheel communicates road feel, while the independent front suspension and rear anti-roll bars allow the truck to settle confidently in quick transitions. Whether merging onto the highway or winding through backroads, the Ram 1500 delivers tactile feedback that rewards attentive driving.

Enthusiasts who prioritize driving enjoyment in a full-size pickup will appreciate this truck's balance of capability and engagement. The Lone Star trim blends the everyday practicality of a spacious cabin and tech-forward features with a driving experience that feels tuned for those who notice steering accuracy, pedal response, and ride composure. Those who see their commute as a chance to savor the road will find the Ram 1500's dynamic feel stands out in the segment.

Performance is a highlight, with the 5.7L V8 HEMI engine delivering assertive throttle response and a muscular exhaust note that complements spirited driving. The 8-speed automatic transmission shifts quickly and smoothly, with manual mode available for those who want to control gear selection on twisty roads or while towing. Steering remains linear and precise, building confidence at speed, while the suspension soaks up rough pavement yet resists body roll, providing a composed and connected feel. Braking is firm and progressive, inspiring trust even during brisk maneuvers or when hauling heavier loads.

Safety systems enhance the driving experience without intruding on driver control. Electronic Stability Control activates seamlessly in low-traction situations, maintaining the truck's intended path without abrupt intervention. Traction control works in the background to keep acceleration smooth, and the ParkView rear backup camera adds confidence in tight spots. ABS brakes deliver consistent, linear stopping power, supporting assertive driving without dulling pedal feel.

The Lone Star trim brings desirable features like a 7.0-inch TFT color driver display for crisp vehicle data, leather-wrapped steering wheel for tactile comfort, and remote start for added convenience. Big Horn Level 1 Equipment Group adds audio upgrades and intuitive controls. Split-folding rear seats and ample storage ensure daily usability, while 18-inch or optional 20-inch alloy wheels enhance both aesthetics and handling. Bluetooth connectivity and Uconnect infotainment keep you engaged and informed on the go.

Against rivals like the Ford F-150 XLT and Chevrolet Silverado RST, the Ram 1500 stands out for steering feel and chassis composure, offering a more connected drive. Where competitors sometimes isolate the driver, this truck communicates the road's subtleties and rewards precise inputs, especially in corners or under heavy load. Its ride quality and interior refinement further set it apart, delivering a rewarding time behind the wheel every day.

Drivers frequently ask whether the Ram 1500 Lone Star is fun to drive, and the answer is yes—the steering is direct, the throttle sharp, and the suspension confidently tuned for both daily commutes and spirited backroad runs.

To experience the engaging drive and tactile feedback of the 2022 Ram 1500 Lone Star, visit Bayway Chevrolet at 5719 Broadway St, Pearland, TX, 77581 or call 281-719-9821. Take the next step toward rewarding time behind the wheel every day with a truck that turns commutes into something you look forward to.

Few small SUVs have built the kind of street-level reputation the TrailBlazer has for threading the needle between city-sized dimensions and a cabin that doesn't feel like a compromise. This particular LT adds real everyday substance to that reputation, with the amplified six-speaker audio system keeping the driver genuinely connected to music and satellite radio on commutes that feel too short to bother with a podcast but too long to sit in silence. Picture yourself pulling into a downtown parking structure on a Thursday evening, sliding into a spot that would have been a squeeze in anything larger, and walking into dinner without giving the car a second thought.

The TrailBlazer's connected services through OnStar and the Chevrolet platform mean that between trips, the car is working in the background even when you're not, whether that's roadside assistance access or remote features that come into play during the kind of week that doesn't slow down. Traction control and four-wheel disc brakes with ABS are easy to ignore until a wet intersection or a sudden stop reminds you they were doing something the whole time, and the front independent suspension keeps that composed, planted feel intact whether the road cooperates or not.

Experience the exceptional blend of style, performance, and safety that the 2023 Kia Sportage EX has to offer. Visit our showroom today and let us demonstrate why this remarkable SUV is the perfect choice for your next adventure.

The 2025 Infiniti QX60 Sensory is a premium three-row luxury SUV that combines family practicality with upscale design and technology. As one of the higher trims in the QX60 lineup, the Sensory model offers a refined interior, advanced safety systems, and enhanced comfort features. It typically starts around the high-$50,000 to low-$60,000 price range depending on drivetrain and options. The SUV seats up to seven passengers and provides a spacious cabin with up to 75.4 cubic feet of cargo capacity when the rear seats are folded, making it suitable for families or long trips.

Under the hood, the 2025 QX60 Sensory is powered by a 2.0-liter turbocharged inline-four engine that produces about 268 horsepower and 286 lb-ft of torque. The engine is paired with a 9-speed automatic transmission and can be configured with either front-wheel drive or all-wheel drive. The vehicle achieves an estimated 22 mpg in the city and around 2728 mpg on the highway, depending on the drivetrain. In addition, it offers a towing capacity of up to 6,000 pounds when properly equipped, making it capable of hauling small trailers or boats.

The Sensory trim stands out for its luxury and technology features. It includes leather seating, heated and ventilated front seats with a massaging function, a 12.3-inch infotainment display, wireless smartphone integration, and a 17-speaker Bose premium sound system. Safety and driver-assistance technologies are also standard, such as blind-spot monitoring, lane-keeping assist, adaptive cruise control, and multiple cameras for parking and visibility. These features help position the 2025 Infiniti QX60 Sensory as a comfortable and technologically advanced SUV in the competitive luxury midsize crossover market.

The 2025 Kia Telluride SX Prestige X-Line is a high-end trim of Kias popular three-row midsize SUV, combining luxury features with rugged styling and enhanced capability. It has a starting MSRP of around $52,785 and comes standard with all-wheel drive as part of the X-Line package. The SUV offers seating for up to seven passengers and provides a spacious interior with up to 87 cubic feet of cargo space when the rear seats are folded. Its elevated ride height, distinctive grille, and black exterior accents give it a more adventurous look compared to other Telluride trims.

Under the hood, the 2025 Telluride SX Prestige X-Line is powered by a 3.8-liter V6 engine that produces 291 horsepower and 262 lb-ft of torque. Unresponsive driver assistant is safety that never sleeps.
Safety and Security
  • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.

Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.
